No catalogue class reads the realsense2_camera_msgs/srv/DeviceInfo identity strings. cap.device.self_test.v1 runs a self-test and cap.sensing.read.v1 is restricted to sensor, sensor.imu and sensor.force_torque resource kinds, not a camera device-info service. The package uses an x-cap id with an inline string output schema for the observation-only service.

No catalogue class returns a camera frame's per-frame metadata JSON text. The metadata topic carries a string, not an image. This original capability returns the color json_data text only; the complete messages with headers are the color/depth metadata extensions.

No catalogue class returns a complete sensor_msgs/msg/CameraInfo message (header, geometry, distortion model, D, K, R, P, binning, ROI); cap.sensing.image.v1 returns pixels only. The package observes the complete color message with an inline schema and ROS 2 wire-range checks, without inferring calibration validity.
The same complete CameraInfo observation for the depth stream (see x-cap.realsenseai.color_camera_info.v1).
No catalogue class returns a camera frame's complete Metadata message: its own header and the exact JSON text, never parsed or reordered.

notes:
Historical author draft below; the final model-review paragraph supersedes its completion claim.

PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached, and no ROS graph, camera, rosbridge connection or hardware run is claimed. RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review at any risk level, so fake evidence does not establish a real ROS or hardware run. The card's family-config decision and RosDriver helper match the C++ ROS 2 topic/service interface, so there is no decision deviation; the card's entry_symbols list is empty, so there was no entry symbol to verify. The driver is configuration-only (no Python native class, no native.py). Scope: three read-verb observations of the default /camera/camera node plus a read-only resource state. x-cap.realsenseai.camera_info.v1 subscribes to /camera/camera/color/camera_info (README.md:631) and maps width, height, header.frame_id, distortion_model, binning_x and binning_y from sensor_msgs/msg/CameraInfo (realsense2_camera/src/rs_node_setup.cpp:309-310). x-cap.realsenseai.device_info.v1 calls the read-only /camera/camera/device_info service (README.md:404, rs_node_setup.cpp:573-574) and maps the seven realsense2_camera_msgs/srv/DeviceInfo strings (realsense2_camera_msgs/srv/DeviceInfo.srv:2-8, filled at rs_node_setup.cpp:640-657). x-cap.realsenseai.frame_metadata.v1 subscribes to /camera/camera/color/metadata (README.md:633) and maps the json_data string of realsense2_camera_msgs/msg/Metadata (rs_node_setup.cpp:368-370, Metadata.msg:1-2). The camera resource reports frame_id, width, height, device_name, serial_number and firmware_version; each field opens its own short subscription or service call and no command is published. The launch file defaults camera_namespace and camera_name to camera (realsense2_camera/launch/rs_launch.py:23-24); README documents the resolved /camera/camera node and endpoints (README.md:379-404). The operator must expose the endpoints that match the deployed graph; the driver follows the README's absolute names and does not guess a namespace or add a remapping. NOT COVERED: image data arrays (color, depth and infrared), the depth point-cloud point array, D/K/R/P calibration matrices, roi and projection parameters, IMU samples and imu_info, extrinsics, the content of the metadata JSON (only its text is returned), /diagnostics, ROS parameter reads or writes, stream enable/disable controls, hw_reset, calib_config_read, calib_config_write, safety-preset services, the triggered_calibration action, and every motion or stop path. The image arrays are what the camera primarily produces; this package exposes the camera's identity and geometry metadata instead, the scalar subset the ROS bridge can carry without copying image arrays, so no fake returns a truncated array and no real array size is claimed. A real deployment must keep the color stream running because the camera_info and metadata topics are published alongside it. hw_reset is not a safety stop: its std_srvs/Empty callback stops the sensors and calls hardware_reset(), catches exceptions with only a warning, and returns an empty response with no application success predicate (rs_node_setup.cpp:614-637), so this package exposes no e-stop and claims no safe state. No numeric input, unit bound, range or writable field is exposed, so there is no Limit, no site-limits.example.json overlay and no SAFE-014 probe; the package is mode hardware at risk R0 (the card floor), matching camera capture as the R0 example in MHS/spec/04-safety.md. The reference's generic software latch is the SDK's no-native-stop state, not a device stop or a safety claim. The fake is a package-local RecordingRosTransport subclass: each outbound subscribe or call_service is answered immediately from canned state, with no wall-clock pacing, physics step [...]
